chunks: A group of scholars narrated to me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, who said: Abu al-Hasan Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Taliqani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us in Dhul-Qa'dah of the year 339 AH: Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mukhallad narrated to us, saying: I was present in Baghdad among the scholars, may Allah bless them. Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may his soul be sanctified, said spontaneously: May Allah have mercy on Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi. The scholars noted the date of that day, and news arrived that he had passed away on that very day. Abu al-Hasan al-Samuri died after that in the middle of Sha'ban in the year 329 AH.

key_terms.أبو الحسن السمري: Abu al-Hasan al-Samuri (a prominent Shia scholar)
key_terms.ابن بابويه: Ibn Babawayh (referring to Ali ibn al-Husayn, father of the scholar)
key_terms.بغداد: Baghdad (city where the event took place)

ai.seo_question: What is the story regarding the death of Ali ibn Babawayh and the praise of al-Samuri?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the spiritual status (*karamat*) of Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, father of the renowned hadith scholar Ibn Babawayh, through the spontaneous praise of the prominent Twelver Imamate representative, Abu al-Hasan al-Samuri. The scholars recorded the date of his praise in Baghdad, and the subsequent arrival of news confirming his death on that very day serves as a traditional sign of his piety and divine favor. This account underscores the continuity of the Imamate’s authority through its representatives and the reverence accorded to the scholarly families of Qom.
